- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5+ points) by overshooting; cap forecast rise to 3–5% above immediate peak.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 10+ consecutive days show upward trend, add 1–2% downward bias to avoid overbought overcorrection.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 2–3 days, not 7–10.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 30% of 30d history mean, model often misses it; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment supports sustained rally.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; use sentiment as momentum multiplier (e.g., +0.1–0.2 to forecast if sentiment > 0.5).
